source: md/1_PRD.md §19 Q1 ('Target days for Scrutiny, Re-Scrutiny, EVC scheduling, SHC, Executive Committee?' — open question for AICTE, line 353) and PRD line 12 (operational thresholds are project proposals, not AICTE rules; Unverified rules stay advisory and never block, return or reject an application).
note: PLACEHOLDER DAY COUNTS — AICTE has not answered §19 Q1, so every number below is a labelled project proposal until a reviewer records the official target days here. The values moved unchanged out of workflow_routes.json (where they rode inline and unlabelled since Phase 1); a pinned test proves the move changed no behaviour. Days are counted from the stage's start (the moment the case entered the stage), and drive visible ageing/escalation only — nothing here gates, returns or rejects a case (DEC-0003). 'days: null' means the prototype deliberately runs no clock for that stage; the note says why.
stage_mapping_note: A stage's day count applies to the states the stage graph (stage_graph.json) maps to it; where two states of one stage count differently (a booked EVC visit vs a held one), the per-state override names the difference. Unmapped states — states the route defines that no PRD stage owns (today: sac_review, whose stage mapping is 3.1's open question) — carry their count under unmapped_state_days rather than pretending to belong to a stage.
unmapped_state_days_note: sac_review's 20 days exist because the route really has that state, but no PRD stage owns it (3.1 open mapping question: SHC? Executive Committee? prototype-only?). The clock is honest about the state without inventing the stage label.
